pages.title: Identifying Fractions
pages.subject: Math
pages.directions: Write the numerator (parts shaded) and denominator (all equal parts). Keep the denominator shown in the picture; you do not need to simplify. Then try the two drawing activities.

items.prompt: What fraction of the whole or set is shaded?
hints: Count all the equal parts or objects for the bottom number.
Count only the shaded parts or objects for the top number.
show: There are 3 parts in all and 2 shaded parts.
items.explain: The numerator counts 2 shaded parts. The denominator counts all 3 parts.
items.retry: The numerator counts shaded or marked parts. The denominator counts ALL equal parts or objects.

mistakes.say: Your numbers are switched. Put the selected number of parts on top and the total number of equal parts on the bottom.

pages.subject: Reading
pages.directions: Use your class paper for the assigned reading. A grown-up listens while you read aloud, counts words read correctly and errors, and records all three attempts. This website does not listen to or automatically score your reading. Follow your teacher’s timing directions; no timing length is printed on the supplied page.

passage.title: A Book Worth Waiting For — original optional practice
passage.text: On Saturday, I carried my library bag into the reading room. A poster announced a new mystery by a writer whose stories always surprised me. I asked for a copy, but every book was already checked out. The librarian offered to put my name on a waiting list. I wanted to discover the ending that afternoon, so I decided to spend some of my saved allowance at the bookstore. Before buying it, I read the first page to make sure the story was right for me. At home, I made a quiet corner beside the window. I placed a cushion on the rug and set a glass of water on a small table. The afternoon light fell across my pages. My brother was playing a noisy game nearby, so I asked if he could move to the kitchen. Soon the room was peaceful. I opened the book and began following the clues. When I finished the first chapter, I stopped to explain the mystery to my brother. He asked to hear more, and we agreed to read the next chapter together.

pages.title: My Favorite Author — Comprehension
pages.subject: Reading
pages.directions: Read your private class passage first. Answer these two classroom tasks in complete sentences and restate the question. A grown-up checks meaning against the class paper. The website checks sentence structure only; it cannot grade your understanding. Responses last only for this visit. Print to keep your work.

items.prompt: Describe the author’s perfect place to read in My Favorite Author.
items.example: The author enjoys a sunny reading spot with a cozy blanket, a pet nearby, and a warm drink.
hints: Restate the question in your own words.
Look back at the class passage for details that explain your answer.
show: Write a complete sentence that answers the question.
The author enjoys a sunny reading spot with a cozy blanket, a pet nearby, and a warm drink.
items.yes: Compare your answer with a grown-up.
items.explain: A grown-up checks that your sentence answers the question using details from the class passage.
